avoid.name: Narrated Reddit threads or articles you didn't write
avoid.why: Listed among formats that get channels demonetized as reused content.

avoid.name: AI doctors, lawyers or money experts
avoid.why: AI personas giving health, legal or financial advice are a named non-monetized category since July 2026.

avoid.name: Shock compilations and fake realistic events
avoid.why: Compilations of unrelated AI clips and realistic footage of events that never happened are being demonetized or removed.

hot.name: Serialized AI microdramas

source.title: YouTube Blog: the evolution of web series on YouTube, microdramas

hot.why: Recurring characters, ongoing plot, a hook ending each episode. YouTube reports microdramas passed 6.5B views in H1 2026, and its Shorts series feature now groups episodes into seasons.

hot.name: AI animal and food-character dramas

source.title: C21Media: AI microdramas set to surge

hot.why: Pet dramas and talking-food soap operas (like the Fruit Love Island format) keep pulling huge view counts; an original cast and a cliffhanger are what carry them.

hot.name: Talking-object explainers

source.title: Miraflow: AI Shorts formats that go viral in 2026

hot.why: An everyday object narrates its own secret in under 45 seconds. Trend guides list talking-object skits among the visual concepts the feed keeps rewarding.

hot.name: What happens to your body
hot.why: Body-science explainers with a curious hook and a checkable payoff; seasonal angles (cold, holidays, sleep) are doing well this month.

hot.name: Untold-story history deep dives
hot.why: Long-form history that zooms in on one specific, little-known story beats broad recaps; one creator reports 2.8x click-through after switching to unsolved-mystery framing.

hot.name: Friend-group POV skits
hot.why: A fixed cast where every character has one clear role; works best as a recurring series rather than one-offs.

doc.angle: How a thriving desert town disappeared in one generation, and what was found when the dunes moved.
doc.title: The Town That Vanished Under Sand

doc.angle: 1816, a volcano half a world away, and the frozen harvests that changed history.
doc.title: The Year Without a Summer

doc.angle: In 1518 hundreds of people danced for weeks; what historians think really happened.
doc.title: The Mystery of the Dancing Plague

explainer.angle: The fridge explains its switch, why it hums at night, and the one shelf that's colder than the freezer.
explainer.hook: Your fridge has been lying to you every time you open it.
explainer.title: Your Fridge Light Has a Secret

explainer.angle: How the nose warms and wets every breath, and why the extra water spills out when it's cold.
explainer.hook: Your nose is a radiator, and winter breaks it.
explainer.title: Why Cold Air Makes Your Nose Run

explainer.angle: Bust the tryptophan myth and reveal what actually knocks you out after a big meal.
explainer.hook: It's not the turkey. It never was.
explainer.title: The Real Reason Turkey Makes You Sleepy

explainer.angle: The battery narrates why heat and 100% charge age it, with one easy habit to fix it.
explainer.hook: Your battery hates the thing you do every night.
explainer.title: What Your Phone Battery Wants You to Know

lstory.angle: A passenger realizes every stop is a year of his own life, and the last one is tonight.
lstory.title: The Night Train to Nowhere

lstory.angle: An original folktale about a bargain, told in chapters with a bittersweet twist.
lstory.title: The Weaver Who Sold Her Shadow

lstory.angle: A survival story where every chapter strips away one more thing the narrator thought they needed.
lstory.title: Seven Days on the Ice

story.angle: A one-eared cat escorts a night-shift nurse home; a photo reveals why he chose her.
story.hook: Every night at 2 a.m., one stray cat waits for the last bus.
story.title: The Stray Who Meets the Last Bus

story.angle: A band of holiday leftovers plots to get eaten before trash day; a midnight snack saves one.
story.hook: In this fridge, Sunday cleanout means nobody gets out alive.
story.title: The Leftovers Have Until Sunday

story.angle: A slow-building winter mystery with a warm twist instead of a scare.
story.hook: Every morning, the snowman is one step closer to my door.
story.title: The Snowman Who Moved One Step

story.angle: An original folktale-style mystery with a twist about who the visitor really is.
story.hook: No boat had come in forty years. Tonight, someone knocked.
story.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Last Visitor

series.premise: A one-eared stray cat escorts a different lonely stranger home every night, and each episode reveals one more clue about who he used to belong to.
series.why: Animal microdramas with a recurring hero and an ongoing mystery are the fastest-growing serialized format.

series.premise: Everyday objects in one apartment confess their secrets, hosted by a grumpy old padlock who has seen it all.
series.why: Talking-object explainers work better with a recurring host character and a running cast.

summary: Serialized, character-led AI content is the strongest lane: YouTube says microdramas passed 6.5B views in the first half of 2026 and Shorts now supports seasons and episodes. Talking-object and body-science explainers keep spreading, while reused-content and fake-expert formats get demonetized.
